name: 四川话 (Sichuanese; 成都 and 重庆 varieties)
summary: Sichuanese is Southwestern Mandarin. Chengdu and Chongqing speech are grouped together but differ in tone values, n/l merger, some vocabulary and the particle system, so name one city per piece. Round 2 added a full-text academic paper on Chongqing sentence-final particles (Tang & Hsu 2024), three Chinese Wikipedia phonology pages (used as pointers, with the cited textbooks named), and about 24 Wiktionary entries that carry Sichuanese labels and Chengdu pinyin. Particle and grammar data come mostly from Chongqing; Chengdu particles (噻, 嘛, 哦, 撒, 嗦) could not be verified and are NOT included. All 'examples' combine verified words or rules unless marked constructed:false.
romanization_note: The 'romanization' fields are toneless pinyin readings, or Sichuan pinyin with tone numbers (1 阴平, 2 阳平, 3 上声, 4 去声) for words taken straight from Wiktionary. They are a reading aid, not a tone-accurate transcription.

grammar.condition: Question word 'what'. Wiktionary lists 啥子 for Southwestern Mandarin (Chengdu, Chongqing, Zigong, Dazhou); Central Plains varieties use 啥 alone. Attested in the film Let the Bullets Fly (2010). Example below is constructed.
How/why question word. The Wiktionary dialect table lists 咋/咋個 for Chengdu and 啷個 for Chongqing. Pick one city and keep it consistent. Example is constructed.
grammar.example_dialect: 这件事咋个办？(重庆：这件事啷个办？)
grammar.romanization: zhe jian shi za go ban / zhe jian shi nang go ban

grammar.condition: Wiktionary's dialect table lists 哪個 (and 啥子人) for 'who' in Chengdu. Ordinary 'which' also exists, so context decides. Example is constructed.
Chengdu lists 沒得, 莫得 and 沒有 as equivalent forms. Verb meaning 'not have'; Chengdu mo2 de2. Example is constructed.
Wiktionary lists 莫 for 'do not' in Chengdu alongside 不要 and 嫑. Short imperative. Example is constructed.

grammar.standard: 好 / 行 / 可以 (OK, fine)
grammar.condition: Adjective or reply meaning 'good, OK, not bad'. Wiktionary labels it dialectal (Southwestern Mandarin, Gan, Xiang); Chengdu yao4 de2. Example is constructed as a reply.
Colloquial verb 'know / understand'. Wiktionary gives Chengdu xiao3 de2. Source 5 uses it in a Chongqing example: 他曉得那個消息lao.

grammar.dialect: lao (Chongqing particle; the paper gives no character)
grammar.condition: Tang & Hsu 2024: Chongqing 'lao' corresponds to sentence-final 了 and sits closest to the clause, before other final particles (lao mai, lao ha, lao suo; never mai lao). The paper writes it in romanization only, so do not guess a character in the script.
grammar.example_dialect: 他晓得那个消息 lao。(paper example)
grammar.romanization: ta xiao de na ge xiao xi lao

grammar.standard: 吃了饭 (completed action, after the verb)
grammar.condition: The same 'lao' also marks a completed action right after the verb. Paper example has both uses in one sentence.
grammar.example_dialect: 他吃 lao 饭 lao。(paper example)

grammar.standard: 吗 (yes/no question, speaker only seeks confirmation)
grammar.condition: Tang & Hsu: 'mai' only asks the hearer to confirm the speaker's own assumption. It cannot be added to wh-questions or A-not-A questions. Paper example: 你讀高中lao mai?
grammar.example_dialect: 你读高中 lao mai？(paper example)
grammar.romanization: ni du gao zhong lao mai

grammar.standard: 吗 (yes/no question, proposition clashes with expectation)
grammar.condition: Tang & Hsu: 'suo' signals that the proposition CONFLICTS with the speaker's presupposition (surprise, doubt). Same ban on wh-questions. The paper gives the frame 他去旅行 lao suo.
grammar.example_dialect: 他去旅行 lao suo？(frame from the paper)
grammar.romanization: ta qu lu xing lao suo

grammar.standard: 吧 / 吗 (yes/no question, proposition fits expectation)
grammar.condition: Tang & Hsu: question 'ha' signals that the proposition AGREES with the speaker's presupposition (like 'right?'). Different from the softener 'ha' below: it cannot follow wh-questions or imperatives.
grammar.example_dialect: 他去旅行 lao ha？(frame from the paper)
grammar.romanization: ta qu lu xing lao ha

grammar.standard: (softener at the end of a question or command)
grammar.condition: Tang & Hsu: a different 'ha' that only softens the tone and can be deleted without changing the sentence type. Works after wh-questions and commands. Their examples: 你看你想吃啥子 ha？/ 你從樹上給我下來 ha！(parent angry but afraid of scaring a child) / 滾開 ha！(warning at a door).
grammar.example_dialect: 你从树上给我下来 ha！(paper example)
grammar.romanization: ni cong shu shang gei wo xia lai ha

grammar.standard: 确实 / 肯定 (speaker is sure)
grammar.condition: Tang & Hsu: 'sa' shows the speaker is certain (epistemic stance). It does not combine with uncertainty words like 大概, 估计, and cannot be used when the speaker sees direct evidence. Examples: 重慶夏天很熱 sa. / 小王肯定沒吃飯 sa. / 李四 sa！
grammar.example_dialect: 重庆夏天很热 sa。(paper example)
grammar.romanization: chong qing xia tian hen re sa

grammar.standard: (reminder of shared background, 'as we both know')
grammar.condition: Tang & Hsu: 'dema' reminds the hearer of background both share, usually something the hearer overlooked. Not allowed in questions. Paper example: 對啊，他上周說他要去北京出差 dema.
grammar.example_standard: 对啊，他上周说他要去北京出差嘛。
grammar.example_dialect: 对啊，他上周说他要去北京出差 dema。(paper example)
grammar.romanization: dui a ta shang zhou shuo ta yao qu bei jing chu chai dema

grammar.standard: verb suffix 倒 (and noun suffix 头)
grammar.dialect: V + 倒 ; 看头, 吃头
grammar.condition: zh.wikipedia 四川话 lists 倒 as a verb suffix (examples 估倒, 马倒) and 头 as a suffix (看头, 吃头). The page names them affixes; I did not read their exact function. Treating 倒 as roughly 着 is common knowledge and needs a native check.

grammar.standard: V得 / V不得 (can / cannot), V起XY
grammar.dialect: special patterns named in the source
grammar.condition: zh.wikipedia 四川话 names these special sentence patterns without full examples. Do not generate sentences with them until a native checks.

grammar.dialect: nouns can be reduplicated; verbs mostly are not
grammar.condition: zh.wikipedia 成都话: nouns can reduplicate, verbs generally do not, unlike Mandarin. Specific forms (e.g. 坝坝) were not verified.

vocabulary.note: Basic question word; Southwestern Mandarin including Chengdu and Chongqing.
Wiktionary table: 咋/咋個 for Chengdu, 啷個 for Chongqing. Pick one per piece.
Chengdu dictionary table gives 哪個 for 'who'; also 啥子人.
Colloquial 'know / understand'.
Chengdu lists 沒得, 莫得, 沒有 as equivalents. A strong Sichuanese marker; use sparingly.
Imperative 'do not' (Chengdu: 莫, 不要, 嫑).
Reply 'OK / fine / not bad'. Very recognizable in film dialogue.
Wiktionary senses: good, suitable, pretty, comfortable, properly done, careful, excellent; also verb 'be close/intimate' and 'to flatter'. Written 巴适 / 巴實 / 粑實.
Standard sense: easy, comfortable. Sichuanese senses listed: healthy, pretty, tasty, satisfied, and also 'awful' (the opposite). Context decides, so avoid it in ambiguous lines.
Chat, gossip, spin a yarn. Wiktionary labels it Southwestern Mandarin: Chengdu, Chongqing, Guiyang, Kunming. 龍門陣 itself = idle talk.
Verb: chat. Listed for Chengdu, Guiyang, Kunming and others.
Sichuan senses: head, brain/mind, and hair (剪脑壳 = get a haircut). Common, warm everyday word.

vocabulary.standard: 伤脑筋 / 头疼 / 难办
vocabulary.note: Rack one's brain; troublesome; annoying (makes one dizzy). Sichuan sense per Wiktionary.
A man meekly subservient to his wife. Teasing, often affectionate; can sting if said to a stranger.
Sichuan interjection 'come on! go!'. WARNING: Wiktionary also lists a vulgar sexual sense (erection). Use only in cheering and only if the scene suits a sports-fan feel.
Child, diminutive. Listed for Chengdu, Guiyang, Nanjing. Often affectionate.
Sichuan: father. In Jin (Taiyuan) the same word means husband, so do not cross-use.
Chengdu: woman or wife. Wiktionary marks it as belittling. Only for a rough-affectionate husband voice.
Wiktionary lists 'beautiful' as a Sichuanese/Xiang sense besides 'clever' and 'well-behaved' (children). Do not read it as 'pretty' by default in Mandarin-like lines.
Sichuan adjective: pitiful, poor thing. The standard Buddhist sense 'to sin' also exists.
INSULT for a foolish person; also an affectionate nickname for a lover or child. Tone and relationship decide. Flag in angry lines.

particles.function: Chongqing sentence-final marker of current relevance, equal to Mandarin sentence-final 了 (change of state, correcting a wrong assumption, progress, closing a statement). Also a verb suffix for completion. The paper writes it as 'lao' only.
particles.example: 他曉得那個消息 lao (he knows that news now)

particles.function: Question particle: asks the hearer to confirm the speaker's own assumption. Not used after wh-words or A-not-A.
Question particle: the proposition clashes with what the speaker presupposed (surprise, doubt).
Question particle: the proposition fits what the speaker presupposed ('right?'). Different from the softener ha.
Softens questions and commands; deletable. Used when the speaker is angry or worried but does not want to sound too harsh.
particles.example: 滾開 ha！ / 你從樹上給我下來 ha！

particles.function: Speaker confirms the proposition is true (certain stance). Cannot go with uncertainty words (大概, 我猜) or direct visible evidence.
particles.example: 重慶夏天很熱 sa。 / 李四 sa！

particles.function: Reminds hearer of shared background information; not used in questions.
particles.example: 對啊，他上周說他要去北京出差 dema。

pronunciation.rule: Retroflex initials are absent: zh/ch/sh become z/c/s (字 = 制). zh.wikipedia 成都话 also says the r initial changes to z. zh.wikipedia 四川话: in the great majority of Sichuan varieties there is no zh/ch/sh set.
pronunciation.actor_tip: Keep the tongue tip flat behind the teeth for zh/ch/sh (say 'zi', 'ci', 'si'). For r- words the source describes z, but this is the least reliable part: have a native confirm before using it on words like 人, 热.
pronunciation.example: 字 = 制 (same sound); 祖 = 主; 愁 = 绸

pronunciation.rule: n and l merge. Chengdu: before open (洪) vowels they merge (納 = 辣, 南 = 藍), before i/ü they stay apart (連 ≠ 年; 力/泥, 吕/女). Chongqing: no separate n-like initial, merging before both kinds of vowels (the page's phrase 洪混细也混).
pronunciation.actor_tip: For Chongqing use an 'l' for most n-words (and l-ish for 年, 女). For Chengdu merge only before a/o/u-type vowels (南, 纳) and keep n before i/ü. Do not apply it to the whole script.
pronunciation.example: 南 = 蓝 (Chengdu); 研 lian, 宜 li (Chongqing, source examples)

pronunciation.rule: Chengdu keeps an ng- initial in many words: 我 ŋo, 硬 ŋən (historical 疑/影 initials).
pronunciation.actor_tip: Start 我 with a nasal 'ng' (ngo) instead of a bare 'wo'. Keep it light.

pronunciation.rule: Entering-tone syllables (short, clipped in older Chinese) merge into tone 2 (阳平), e.g. 七 = 齐. No yin/yang split in the departing tone (士 = 四 = 事).
pronunciation.actor_tip: Words like 七, 不, 吃, 一 are said as 2nd-tone words (low, value 21), not clipped.
pronunciation.example: 七 = 齐; 士 = 四 = 事

pronunciation.rule: No distinction between 尖 and 团 sounds: 绝 = 决 in Chengdu.
pronunciation.actor_tip: Nothing to add: say both as the same j-type sound.

pronunciation.rule: Some words keep a hard g/k/h initial where Mandarin has j/q/x: 街 gai1, 鞋 hai2, 螃蟹 kai4, 巷子 hang4 (listed on the Chongqing page in its own spelling).
pronunciation.actor_tip: Say 街 as 'gai' and 鞋 as 'hai'. Use in everyday words only, not formal or abstract speech.
pronunciation.example: 街 gai; 鞋子 hai zi

pronunciation.rule: Chongqing vs Chengdu rhyme difference: Chengdu 欲 yo, 俗 xyo; Chongqing 欲 yu, 俗 xyu. The Chongqing page counts it as one of only two main phonological differences apart from exceptional words.
pronunciation.actor_tip: For a Chongqing setting, say 欲 and 俗 with a clear 'yu'.

pronunciation.rule: Erhua exists in Chengdu but lighter than in Beijing or the Northeast; examples on the page: 凉粉儿, 饭碗儿, 抽签儿, 公园儿.
pronunciation.actor_tip: Add a soft r-ending only on small nouns like those; do not r-ify every noun.

tones_intonation.rule: Chengdu (zh.wikipedia 四川话): 阴平 45, 阳平 21, 上声 42, 去声 213. zh.wikipedia 成都话 gives 去声 as 24 in a 1941 survey and 13 in the main text, so check the fourth tone with a native speaker.
Chongqing: 阴平 55, 阳平 21, 上声 42, 去声 214. So Chongqing 1st tone is high level; Chengdu 1st tone rises slightly (45).
All old entering-tone syllables join 阳平 (tone 2) in both cities. There are four tones and no short clipped syllables.

Tone change in Chengdu (zh.wikipedia 成都话): a 阴平 before another 阴平 becomes 55; a 阳平 before any syllable becomes 22; a 上声 before any syllable becomes 44. Treat as a guide only; the page does not say how audible this is.

Chongqing final particles carry the attitude: a softening 'ha' in anger (warning a child), 'sa' to confirm, 'dema' to remind. Keep them short, at the end of the phrase, and do not stack more than one per sentence.

examples.note: 啥子는 쓰촨·충칭 공통의 '무엇'. 규칙을 조합한 문장이라 원어민 확인 필요.

examples.romanization: zhe jian shi za go ban / nang go ban

晓得는 일상 구어. 부정은 표준어 不를 그대로 쓴 조합.

莫 = 不要. 위로할 때는 낮고 부드럽게.
청두 표에서 哪个가 '누구'. 문맥으로 '어느'와 구분.

examples.romanization: zou qu bai long men zhen
examples.note: 摆龙门阵 = 한가한 잡담. 청두·충칭 대표 표현.

examples.korean_idea: 저 사람은 아내한테 꼼짝 못 해.(놀림)
examples.romanization: ta shi ge pa er duo
examples.note: 耙耳朵 = 공처가. 놀림이지만 애정 섞인 경우가 많다.

examples.romanization: zhe jian shi hao da nao ke
examples.note: 打脑壳 = 골치 아프다. '好'(아주)는 표준어에서 가져온 조합.

examples.korean_idea: 당장 나무에서 내려와!(화나지만 겁주기 싫을 때)
examples.regional: 你从树上给我下来 ha！
examples.romanization: ni cong shu shang gei wo xia lai ha
examples.note: 끝의 ha는 명령을 부드럽게 하는 충칭 표지(논문 예문). 화난 어조는 유지.

examples.romanization: ta xiao de na ge xiao xi lao
examples.note: lao = 了. 논문 예문. 논문에 한자 표기가 없어 로마자로 둔다.
논문 예문(집 앞 침입자에게 경고). 수위가 높으니 장면이 허락할 때만.

examples.romanization: ni zhe ge gua wa zi
examples.note: 瓜娃子는 욕도, 애칭도 된다. 관계에 맞는 억양 선택.

sub_regions.features: Tones 45/21/42/213 per the tone table; n/l merge before open vowels but not before i/ü; yo rhyme (欲 yo); 咋个 for 'how/why'; ng- initial for 我, 硬; light erhua.

Tones 55/21/42/214; n/l merge before all vowels; yu rhyme (欲 yu); 啷个 for 'how/why'; rich final-particle system (lao, mai, suo, ha, sa, dema). zh.wikipedia 重庆话 says that apart from some exceptional words there are only two main phonological differences from Chengdu, even though listeners hear them as quite different.
Wiktionary marks 巴适, 安逸, 要得, 晓得, 莫得 as Southwestern Mandarin or Chengdu words. Whether each is used identically in Chongqing was not verified. Use with care.

common_mistakes: Mixing Chengdu and Chongqing markers in one script (e.g. 咋个 and 啷个, or applying Chongqing's full n/l merger to a Chengdu character).
Putting 巴适, 安逸, 要得, 莫得, 啥子 in every line. Use 1 to 3 per paragraph in casual speech only.
Reading 安逸 or 乖 as plain 'comfortable / pretty': the Sichuanese senses (安逸 can mean 'awful'; 乖 can mean 'beautiful') change the meaning.
Using 雄起 outside cheering: Wiktionary lists a vulgar sexual sense too.
Using 瓜娃子 or 婆娘 as casual flavor. 瓜娃子 can be an insult or a pet name; 婆娘 is belittling. 龟儿子 was not verified at all, so it is excluded.
Curling the tongue for zh/ch/sh/r. These sounds are absent in Chengdu and most Sichuanese.
Making up particles. Only Chongqing lao, mai, suo, ha, sa, dema are verified, and the paper gives them in romanization only.
Copying the Mandarin tone shapes. Sichuan has four tones with no entering tone, and its tone values differ from Beijing.
generational_notes: Tang & Hsu 2024 do not report age differences. No verified source on older vs younger Sichuanese vocabulary was found.
The English Wikipedia (source 1, round 1) calls 雄起 a newer urban word; Wiktionary lists it as a cheering interjection. Whether it sounds natural to a current Chengdu speaker is still unverified.
zh.wikipedia 四川话 mentions that younger speakers lose some initials (nʲ, ŋ). Details are in the source and were not verified for acting use.
conversion_guidelines: Step 1: pick Chengdu or Chongqing from the brief. If unspecified, default to Chengdu and say so in the note.
Write natural film-dialogue Mandarin first, then replace only verified items: 什么→啥子, 怎么→咋个 (Chengdu) / 啷个 (Chongqing), 谁→哪个, 知道→晓得, 没有→莫得, 别→莫, 好的→要得, 聊天→摆龙门阵, 头→脑壳.
Keep Mandarin word order. Sichuanese grammar beyond the items in 'grammar' was not verified, so do not invent constructions.

Final particles: for Chongqing you may add 'lao' (=了), 'ha' (softener), 'sa' (certainty) or 'dema' (reminder) as in the paper, written in romanization or marked for native review since the paper gives no characters. For Chengdu add none until verified.
Use at most 1 to 3 regional words per paragraph. Do not use 瓜娃子, 婆娘 or 雄起 unless the character, relationship and scene clearly allow it, and flag them.
Give actors tone notes from the tone table (Chengdu 45/21/42/213; Chongqing 55/21/42/214) and the 'no zh/ch/sh/r' tip, not invented intonation.
Mark constructed lines as constructed and ask a Chengdu or Chongqing native to check them before performance.

open_questions: Chengdu sentence-final particles (噻, 嘛, 哦, 撒, 嗦, 喃) were not verified. Search results pointed to theses (陈振宁 2018 Zhejiang U., 林凌 2007 Jilin U., 赵媛媛 2006 Sichuan U.) said to cover Chengdu particles; their content was not opened. Check CNKI.
Tang & Hsu use romanization (lao, mai, suo, ha, sa, dema) and give no characters. Ask Chongqing speakers which characters they write (e.g. 咯, 嘛, 嗦, 撒, 嘚嘛).
Chengdu 4th tone value: zh.wikipedia 成都话 gives 24 (1941 survey) and 13 (main text) while zh.wikipedia 四川话 gives 213. Needs a phonetic source.
Whether Chengdu r- is really z-like (zh.wikipedia 成都话 says ʐ becomes z) and which words are affected.
龟儿子 was not looked up. For 瓜娃子 only Wiktionary's one-line register label was found.
硬是, 恼火, 撇脱, 好耍, 板扎: looked up but Wiktionary gave no Sichuanese label or the page was missing, so not used.
Chongqing vs Chengdu usage of 巴适, 安逸, 晓得, 莫得 not separately verified.
Ask a native to check at least these constructed lines: 莫得钱, 莫哭了, 哪个来了, 这件事好打脑壳.
confidence_note: low-to-medium (Chongqing particles: medium, one peer-reviewed paper; Chengdu vocabulary: medium, dictionary entries; Chengdu particles: none verified)
